name: Mahatma Gandhi Expressway
history: The Ahmedabad–Vadodara Expressway, officially the Mahatma Gandhi Expressway, was one of India's first access-controlled expressways when it fully opened in 2004. Numbered National Expressway 1 (NE-1), it runs beside the older Ahmedabad–Vadodara highway but with no crossings or slow traffic, cutting the trip between the two cities to about an hour. It passes through the Kheda and Anand districts, the heart of Gujarat's dairy country, and today it also links up with the new Delhi–Mumbai Expressway corridor near Vadodara.
facts: India's first road to carry the 'National Expressway' number: NE-1.
Cut the Ahmedabad–Vadodara drive to about an hour.
Passes through the Anand district, famous as the home of Amul dairy.
Opened in 2004, two years after the Mumbai–Pune Expressway.
